criteria.check: Read metrics.py, graph.py draft/guard nodes and llm.py; confirmed every figure is computed in metrics.compute and the model only receives the rendered table. Guard weaknesses are recorded under R4, not here.
Read every Metric(...) evidence list in metrics.py; ran tests/test_metrics.py::test_evidence_reproduces_each_figure (passes for all 9 archetype x profile cases).
Read graph.draft: the user prompt holds the account name (always 'Applicant'), the period, metrics.as_table and the policy rules. No transaction rows are included.

Checked redraft routing (max 2, then review marked ungrounded) and probed guard.check with adversarial memos. Routing is correct, but the guard grounds wrong counts in the 0-31 range, sign-flipped values and wrong-unit values.
Read graph.review/_review_problem, ReviewDecision and cli.run. Ran the CLI with --reviewer '   ' --yes and it approved with a blank name.
Read categorise.RULES and probed with an owner capital injection and an HMRC VAT repayment received by FPS. Both were categorised as revenue_transfer instead of other.

Read policy/uk_sme_default.yaml and policy.evaluate: thresholds and pass/refer/fail outcomes come from YAML. Calculation constants such as the VAT window stay in code, but those are metric definitions, not lending policy.

Grepped committed CSV/JSON/MD/PY for personal, employer and account identifiers; listed the distinct descriptions in examples/ and evals/results/statements. All data is generated by synth.py and the counterparties are fictional (one real carrier name, PARCELFORCE WORLDWIDE, appears as a supplier label only).

Read ingest.load_csv: missing columns, unparseable dates, non-finite amounts, inconsistent balances and duplicate ids are each refused. A probe showed that a valid but out-of-sequence date passes the file-order balance walk and is then silently re-sorted, which changes M1 and the policy outcome.
Read .github/workflows/ci.yml and llm.get_llm (defaults to fake); ran python3 -m pytest -q locally: 94 passed with no key set.

Property probe over 4320 statements (3 archetypes x 3 profiles x 40 seeds x 4 end dates x 6/12/24 months) comparing M2, M5, M6, M7, M8, M11 and M12 to ground truth. 13 cases fail on M5; the suite only tests seed 7 with one end date.
Probed guard.check: '48250GBP' and spelled-out amounts are never scanned, so a non-derivable number is not flagged.

findings.claim: A bare integer from 0 to 31 that equals no metric is exempt, and that range covers every policy-driving count (M1, M6, M7, M13). The memo can misstate returned direct debits or days overdrawn and still be graded grounded. R4 has no such exemption; the P2 carve-out contradicts R4 for exactly the numbers the policy decides on.
findings.repro: Metrics M7=5 (returned DDs), M6=27, M1=12. guard.check('There were 2 returned direct debits and the account was overdrawn on 3 days [M1].', M).grounded -> True (policy rule R3 threshold is 2).

findings.claim: _matches accepts +/- the metric value, and line 79 matches against every metric regardless of unit. The memo can reverse the sign of a balance or cash flow, or quote a metric in the wrong unit, and pass.
findings.repro: M5=-3200, M9=-12000, M1=12 (months). 'The lowest balance was a healthy £3,200 [M5] in credit.' -> grounded True; 'Net operating cash flow was a positive £12,000 [M9].' -> True; 'Revenue grew 12% [M1] year on year.' -> True.

findings.claim: Days overdrawn counts only dates on which a transaction happened, not calendar days the closing balance was negative, as the M6 method claims. An account overdrawn for 17 days with no activity scores 1, which can turn policy rule R4 (fewer than 15 days) from refer into pass. P1 cannot catch this because synth.py:219-220 uses the same definition.
findings.repro: CSV, opening balance 1000: 2026-01-03 FASTER PAYMENT SUPPLIER -1500 (balance -500); 2026-01-20 CARD SETTLEMENT +2000. compute() -> M6 = 1 (true value 17).

findings.claim: VAT lateness assumes every business pays on the 1st-11th of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct. Only one of HMRC's three stagger groups is due then; the others are due on the 7th of Feb/May/Aug/Nov or Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec. On a real lender statement, on-time VAT is counted late and refers rule R5. A business that pays no VAT at all gets M13=0 and passes. The synth generator (synth.py:189-196) shares the assumption, so evals cannot see it.
findings.repro: Four 'HMRC VAT' debits on 2026-02-07, 05-07, 08-07, 11-07 (on time for stagger 1) -> M13 = 4. A statement with no VAT payments -> M13 = 0.

findings.claim: The '^FPS CREDIT|^BACS CREDIT' alternatives classify every inbound Faster Payment or BACS credit as customer revenue based on the payment rail alone: owner capital injections, inter-account transfers, HMRC refunds, grants. That is a guess, not a rule match. It inflates M2, M3, M9 and M10 (DSCR).
findings.repro: Credits 'FPS CREDIT J SMITH CAPITAL INJECTION' 25000 and 'FPS CREDIT HMRC VAT REPAYMENT' 4000 -> both revenue_transfer; M2 = 29000.

findings.claim: The counterparty key is description words 2-4. For two-word payer names that includes the per-payment invoice number, so one customer becomes many and top-customer share (M15) is understated. Policy rule R7 then passes a fully concentrated book. This happens in the repo's own synthetic data (OAKFIELD PROPERTIES, T WHITTAKER, RIVERSIDE LETTINGS; and 'S & K PATEL' is truncated to 'S & K').
findings.repro: Ten credits 'FPS CREDIT OAKFIELD PROPERTIES INV1000..1009', 1000 each -> M15 = 10.0 (true value 100).

findings.claim: reviewer has min_length=1 without stripping, so a whitespace-only name is a valid identity. cli.py:50 checks truthiness only. The C6 fix was proven only against '' and a missing key (tests/test_graph.py:169).
findings.repro: cma run <stmt.csv> --reviewer '   ' --yes --out memo.md -> exit 0, stamp 'APPROVED by     at 2026-11-07 23:11 UTC.'

findings.claim: The balance walk (line 77) is validated in file order, then rows are re-sorted by date. A row with a valid but wrong date (a typo) passes, lands in another month, and changes the metrics. The validated sequence is not the one computed from.
findings.repro: synth.generate('cafe','good',end=2026-09-30,months=11); set the last row's date to 2062-09-30; load_csv accepts it; M1 = 12 and policy rule R1 (twelve months) -> pass instead of refer.

findings.claim: Lowest balance ignores the opening balance, which can be derived from the first row (balance - amount). Ground truth (synth.py:214) includes it, so P1 fails in 13 of 4320 generated statements. The tests only use seed 7, which never hits this.
The negative lookahead rejects a number glued to letters, and the regex then backtracks to no match at all, so '48250GBP' or '£48,250pa' are never checked. Spelled-out amounts are not scanned either.
findings.repro: guard.check('Stock is worth 48250GBP according to the owner [M2].', M).grounded -> True; same for 'forty-eight thousand pounds'.

findings.claim: Citations are checked per sentence, not per number, so swapping two figures' labels passes. This defeats the bet outcome '(b) cites every figure'.
findings.repro: M2=120000, M8=30000: 'Total revenue was £30,000 [M8] and debt service was £120,000 [M2].' -> grounded True.

findings.claim: The rounding tolerance scales with the suffix, so '£0m' matches any metric with an absolute value below £500,000.

The draft prompt includes policy thresholds (policy.py:43 'rule requires >= 1.25') and tells the model to explain referred or failed rules. The guard flags those thresholds as ungrounded, so a faithful real-model memo will habitually need a reviewer override, which wears down the control.
findings.repro: guard.check('Debt service cover of 1.42 [M10] against a policy minimum of 1.25x.', metrics with M10=1.42) -> unmatched ['1.25x'].

findings.claim: ci.yml:22-23 says the eval job fails if any computed metric disagrees with ground truth, but run_evals only compares M2 (line 58). The claim is wider than its proof.
findings.repro: Read run_evals.py:58 and :72; no other metric is compared.
